title: The AI Boom Is Creating Blue Collar Millionaires (3 Stocks You'll Wish You Bought)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: In "The AI Boom Is Creating Blue Collar Millionaires (3 Stocks You'll Wish You Bought)," published 4 Oct 2026, MarketBeat hosts guest Rob Spibbey of Altimetry, who pitches data-center infrastructure plays — the physical, blue-collar side of the AI buildout that the market hasn't priced. He makes three BUY calls with no stated prices: EME (EMCOR, electrical/HVAC) — roughly half of revenue comes from data centers and backlog grew from $12B to $17B, with the market not pricing the next few years of growth; DY (Dycom fiber-optic contractor) — down ~45% in three months on capex-question fears; and URI (United Rentals equipment rental). The digest notes the EME ticker was corrected in the run after captions garbled it as "MCOR" (verified NYSE:EME). These are guest picks framed as infrastructure beneficiaries of the AI boom rather than the hyperscaler/software side. No prior calls were recorded for these names, so there are no flips.

calls.thesis: Emcor, electrical/HVAC contractor: half of revenue from data centers; backlog grew $12B to $17B (~50%) and blue-collar workforce from 34k to 44k; market is not pricing the next few years of growth.
calls.base: Hyperscaler capex $800B this year toward $1.2T; skilled-labor bottleneck (500k-1M more electricians needed) keeps revenue opportunity durable.
calls.bear: AI-capex air pocket (election-year NIMBYism narrative) has already dragged AI-infrastructure names down 20-30%.

calls.thesis: Dycom, fiber-optic contractor for telecoms now also building data-center power solutions: US rural-fiber mandate plus dark-fiber exhaustion; down ~45% in 3 months on capex-question fears.
calls.base: Rural-fiber buildout + data-center power work + replacement cycle in fiber; growth over next 3 years not priced in.
calls.bear: Same AI-capex narrative overhang; chart looks ugly and the drawdown could continue if capex fears persist.

calls.thesis: United Rentals, equipment rental: needs equipment to build data centers, power plants and fiber; benefits from broader reshoring/nearshoring capex too; market prices earnings flat vs 2023-24, missing the story.
calls.base: Capex $200B to $465B to $800B trajectory plus specialty-rental scale/moat (12% ROA on uniform basis); he calls it '100% a buying opportunity'.
calls.bear: Equipment rental is cyclical; a capex slowdown would hit utilization and pricing.
